links.outcome: Autism classification performance when low-confidence AI features were deferred to human annotators versus AI-only
links.effect: Aggregate out-of-fold AUROC 0.76 for HITL multimodal model vs 0.54 for AI-only; mean sensitivity rose from 0.51 to 0.66 as 59.7% of frames were replaced by human annotation. Exploratory, non-causal.
links.quote: The HITL-enhanced multimodal model achieved an aggregate out-of-fold AUROC of 0.76, compared with 0.54 for the AI-only model.

links.outcome: autism classification sensitivity after human replacement
links.effect: At threshold 0.9, 59.7% (597/1000) frames were human-replaced; sensitivity increased from 0.51 (SD 0.24) to 0.66 (SD 0.10).
links.quote: At a threshold of 0.9, 59.7% (597/1000) of frames were replaced by human annotations, and mean sensitivity increased from 0.51 (SD 0.24) at a threshold of 0.1 to 0.66 (SD 0.10) at a threshold of 0.9, an absolute increase of approximately 15 percentage points.
